chunks: [Fulfilment of Trust :] Then, as regards fulfilment of trust, whoever does not pay attention to it will be disappointed.
It was placed before the strong skies, vast earths and high mountains but none of them was found to be stronger. vaster, or higher than it.
If anything could be unapproachable because of height, vastness, power or strength they would have been unapproachable,
but they felt afraid of the evil consequences (of failure in fulfilling a trust) and noticed what a weaker being did not realise it, and this was man.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'Trust' (Amanah) offered to the heavens and earth in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha elaborates on the cosmic significance of 'Amanah' (Trust), contrasting the physical grandeur of the heavens, earth, and mountains with the spiritual capacity of humanity. It highlights that while creation declined due to fear of accountability, humans accepted the burden despite their inherent weakness and ignorance, a duality reflected in the Quranic description of man as 'ظَلُومًا جَهُولًا' (wrongful and ignorant). This acceptance establishes the foundation for human moral agency and divine testing within Shia theological discourse.
